Two changes follow. Aggregation is changed from max to median, so a single worst-case study no longer defines a candidate that has several. operational_quantity.quantity_name: Change in exposure with gastric acid suppression

matching_facets.statement: the four facets of the recovery rubric (handoff §12.2), read from executing fields; `gaps` lists what the records do not say

meaning.definition: The magnitude of the percentage change in systemic exposure (AUC) when the compound is co-administered with an acid-reducing agent, taken from a dedicated interaction study and entered as a non-negative number: a 53 percent fall enters as 53 and a 13 percent fall as 13, and a rise of the same size enters identically. The sign of the change, the class of acid-reducing agent and the formulation studied are recorded alongside the value but are not scored, so the predicate orders candidates by how far exposure moves and never ranks a larger loss as better than a smaller one. Smaller magnitude is better. Where no dedicated study exists the attribute returns unknown, which carries no penalty and leaves the candidate unranked on this attribute rather than scored as insensitive; where the source describes the compound as a weak base with pH-dependent solubility that liability is recorded as an annotation for a later stage to read, not converted into a score, because this evidence supports no number for it. Because the magnitude depends on the salt form, solid-state form and excipients of the product studied, a value may not be transferred between formulations.
meaning.expected_change: Candidates with a dedicated study showing little change rank above candidates with a large measured reduction, in either direction of effect, while candidates with no study are unranked on this attribute and carry a recorded pH-dependence annotation for a later stage rather than a score.
meaning.falsification_test: List which candidates have a dedicated acid-suppression study. If most candidates are unranked the attribute discriminates little and the recorded annotations, not the score, carry the dimension; if the recorded pH-dependence annotations turn out to predict the measured magnitudes well, a later iteration can propose a scored quantity for them on evidence this request does not contain.
meaning.rationale: The cited quotes establish both the mechanism and the spread of measured magnitudes. A majority of orally administered molecularly targeted agents are weak bases with pH-dependent solubility whose absorption is impaired by acid suppression, described as a potential Achilles heel of targeted therapy, and acid-reducing agents are among the most commonly used medicines in the oncology population. For weakly basic compounds solubility is highest in the acidic fasted stomach, so loss of gastric acidity reduces the fraction dissolved. Measured effects run from no clinically meaningful change, through a 41 percent fall in peak concentration with only 13 percent in AUC, to AUC reductions of 43 and 53 percent, and one quote records that the same agent is judged differently by two regulators. Because every measured value is a reduction while the mechanism admits either direction, the quantity is the unsigned magnitude and the sign is recorded, so the ordering cannot invert. A further quote ties the magnitude to the formulation studied, which is why the definition forbids transferring values between products. Nothing in the cited evidence states an acceptable magnitude, so the rule is an ordering with no cutoff, and nothing in it supports a numeric penalty for an untested compound, which is why the pH-dependence liability is recorded rather than scored.

operational_quantity.unit: % of dose recovered by the predominant route

matching_facets.statement: the four facets of the recovery rubric (handoff §12.2), read from executing fields; `gaps` lists what the records do not say

meaning.definition: The percentage of the administered dose recovered by the single predominant excretory route in a mass-balance study, with the recovery by the other route recorded alongside: a compound recovering 65 percent of the dose in faeces and 25 percent in urine scores 65, and one recovering 42 percent in faeces and 22 percent in urine scores 42. A high value means elimination is concentrated in one route and the compound's clearance therefore depends on one organ's function; a lower value means the routes share it. Lower is better. Only a stated recovery percentage is entered. A source stating only that elimination is mainly by one route, without a percentage for it, yields unknown with that statement and any percentage it does give for the minor route recorded, because the share carried by the predominant route cannot be inferred from the minor route's share when recovery is incomplete. A route-of-clearance fraction, such as a statement of what percentage of the drug undergoes renal clearance, is a different quantity and is recorded with its own description rather than entered, because recovery of the administered dose and apportionment of clearance are not interchangeable. The quantity is one number rather than a split, so the predicate has a monotone order; the full split remains in the record for a later stage to read.
meaning.expected_change: Candidates whose elimination is shared between routes rank above candidates that funnel almost the whole dose through one, so a candidate whose single clearance route is removed by impairment of one organ is visibly disfavoured, and the recorded split explains the organ-impairment dose rules scored separately.
meaning.falsification_test: If mass-balance recoveries are unavailable for most candidates this attribute is inert and the organ-impairment dose-adjustment attributes carry the same information in a coarser form. If a candidate's predominant-route share is low only because its mass-balance recovery was incomplete, the value is an artefact of recovery and must be routed to a human rather than scored as redundancy.
meaning.rationale: The cited quotes give elimination balances for agents of this class and show that concentration in one route creates a dependency on one organ: one agent recovers 65 percent of the dose in faeces and 25 percent in urine, another 42 percent in faeces and 22 percent in urine, and a third is reported as mainly excreted in faeces with less than 1 percent eliminated in urine, which states the minor route's share but not the predominant route's and therefore yields unknown on this axis with the statement recorded. Those splits are what make organ function a determinant of exposure for some agents of this class and not others, which is the consequence the organ-impairment attributes score directly. Scoring the share carried by the predominant route, rather than a two-number split or a window with no stated bounds, gives a single monotone axis that the evidence supports, and only percentages the sources state are entered, so the worked examples are exactly the two quotes that report both routes numerically. No cited quote states an acceptable renal or faecal percentage, so there is no cutoff and no range. A quote stating a renal function threshold for dosing, and one apportioning clearance rather than reporting recovery, are not cited here, because neither reports a mass-balance recovery.

matching_facets.statement: the four facets of the recovery rubric (handoff §12.2), read from executing fields; `gaps` lists what the records do not say

meaning.definition: The upper bound of the 90 percent confidence interval of the estimated mean QTc change, in milliseconds, at the highest exposure the source models, with that exposure recorded alongside: where a source reports bounds at the steady-state clinical peak concentration and at a multiple of it, the bound at the multiple is the admitted value and the clinical-exposure bound is recorded. The axis is defined at the highest modelled exposure, rather than at the clinical exposure alone, for two reasons: it is the conservative figure, since a candidate's exposure can rise with an interacting co-medication, and it is the figure these sources report as the headline estimate, so the admitted value is the one the source itself carries and no reader has to reconstruct a different one. A value estimated from a concentration-QTc model is recorded as model-derived. A candidate for which the evidence offers only event counts, a symptom list or a monitoring instruction returns unknown rather than a value, and reported rates of cardiac failure, left ventricular dysfunction and ischaemic events are percentages, a different quantity that is recorded rather than entered and is scored, where quantified, by the severe-adverse-event attribute. Where candidates' bounds come from different exposure multiples the multiple is recorded with each value, and because a bound estimated at a higher multiple is the more conservative figure, an ordering that prefers the candidate whose bound was estimated at the higher multiple errs on the side of caution rather than against the candidate. Smaller QT effect is better.
meaning.expected_change: Candidates with a documented negligible modelled QT effect rank above candidates with a larger estimated effect, the admitted number is the one the source reports with its exposure recorded, and candidates with only event or monitoring content return unknown rather than a fabricated value.
meaning.falsification_test: A negligible QT effect measured at the approved dose does not exclude an effect at higher exposure or with an interacting co-medication; if the only data are at a single dose level the attribute must be read together with the interaction attributes.
meaning.rationale: One cited quote gives this quantity directly: a concentration-QTc model estimated the upper bounds of the 90 percent confidence interval of the mean QTc change as 0.0537 milliseconds at the steady-state peak concentration and 4.00 milliseconds at twice that concentration, and 4.00 is the figure the claim itself carries as its value with the unit in milliseconds. Defining the axis at the highest modelled exposure therefore makes the admitted number the one the source and the claim both report, instead of a figure that has to be read back out of the quote, and it is also the conservative choice for a compound whose exposure can be raised by an interacting co-medication. The quote also makes plain that the figure is model-derived, which the definition records rather than conceals. No cited quote states an acceptable QT effect, so the rule is an ordering with no cutoff, and a negligible modelled effect does not exclude an effect at exposures beyond those modelled, which is why the recorded exposure multiple and the interaction attributes must be read with it.

matching_facets.statement: the four facets of the recovery rubric (handoff §12.2), read from executing fields; `gaps` lists what the records do not say

meaning.definition: The median expert-curated affinity of the compound at the colony-stimulating-factor-1 receptor, on the pChEMBL scale, that is the negative base-ten logarithm of the molar half-maximal inhibitory concentration, inhibition constant or dissociation constant as the curation reports it. Higher is better. The source bound here is an expert curation independent of the activity table that the registry's potency criterion for this receptor reads, and it can cover compound-target pairs that table lacks, which is the gap this attribute is for: a candidate whose engagement of this receptor is absent from one curation may be quantified in the other. It is therefore not a restatement of the registry criterion and does not replace it. The two read different sources, the median is taken over the records this source returns rather than a maximum, because a maximum rises with the number of records, and the action type and any selectivity comment travel with each record for a narrative to cite. Where the two curations disagree materially about the same compound the conflict is routed to a human rather than averaged. Absence of a record gives unknown and never a failure, because this curation is sparse outside developed and late-stage drugs.
meaning.expected_change: Candidates whose affinity at this receptor is quantified by a curation independent of the activity table are ranked on that measurement, which recovers coverage evidence for candidates the activity table does not cover, while candidates with no record in either curation are not penalised.
meaning.falsification_test: Compare this curation's values with the registry potency criterion for the same receptor across the pool. If the two agree everywhere and cover the same candidates, this attribute adds nothing and should be merged into that criterion; if they disagree materially for a candidate, the conflict is routed to a human rather than averaged. If the curation returns no record for any candidate the attribute yields only unknowns.
meaning.rationale: The objective requires that one molecule engage this microenvironmental receptor, and the cited quotes establish that it is a clinically drugged target with an approved oral inhibitor, that it belongs to the receptor protein-tyrosine kinase families alongside the other required receptors, that single agents documented to cover it together with the vascular receptors exist, that co-inhibiting it with the vascular receptors is rationalised as relieving receptor-driven immune suppression, and that a compound should be regarded as a pathway modulator rather than a confirmed inhibitor where direct biochemical inhibition was never reported. The mechanism-of-action record source this attribute previously read stamps every claim it returns with determination basis curated, a basis excluded by the bases an attribute here accepts, so every record it returned would be set aside at assessment time and the attribute would carry no evidence at all; that is the finding this revision answers. The attribute is therefore bound instead to the independent expert curation of affinity at this receptor, which returns measured values on the pChEMBL scale and, being independent of the activity table, reaches compound-target pairs that table lacks, the same gap the record-based form was meant to close, while stating how strongly rather than only that engagement is documented. No cited quote states a required affinity at this receptor, so the rule is an ordering with no cutoff, and an absent record is unknown rather than a failure.

meaning.expected_change: Candidates inside the stated lipophilicity band score zero and are not separated on this attribute, while both excessively lipophilic and excessively polar candidates are demoted in proportion to their distance outside it.
meaning.falsification_test: If the ranking by this computed proxy inverts the ranking by measured oral bioavailability, the neutral-species descriptor is the wrong quantity for these molecules, as the cited source itself implies, and the attribute must be withdrawn in favour of the measured value.
meaning.rationale: The cited quote states that moderate lipophilicity, typically a logP of about 2 to 4, is considered optimal for this class because it permits passive membrane diffusion without excessively compromising aqueous solubility. The two failure modes are quoted separately and are now both encoded by the two-sided quantity: compounds of excessively high lipophilicity show poor aqueous solubility, increased metabolic clearance and higher affinity for efflux transporters, while highly polar low-logP molecules show limited membrane permeability. Two further cited quotes show the same parameter driving transporter behaviour, with efflux activity particularly sensitive to lipophilicity and halogen substitution raising lipophilicity at the cost of greater efflux susceptibility, which is why the band and not a direction is the right form. The deprecation of the neutral-species descriptor in favour of logD is recorded above as a declared limitation rather than left implicit.

meaning.definition: The percentage reduction in systemic exposure (AUC) when the compound is co-administered with a strong CYP3A inducer, entered as a non-negative percentage of the exposure without the inducer. A loss reported as a fold is converted before entry: a reduction of F-fold enters as (1 minus 1 divided by F) times 100 percent, so a roughly 10-fold loss of exposure enters as approximately 90 percent, and no value may be entered as a bare fold. A reported change in apparent oral clearance, and a peak-concentration change, are different endpoints and are recorded rather than entered on this axis. Only an administered interaction study yields a value; a model-based projection is recorded as a prediction. Smaller losses are better, because loss of exposure is loss of target coverage.
meaning.expected_change: Candidates robust to enzyme induction rank above candidates that lose most of their exposure to a common anticonvulsant, antimicrobial or herbal product, which is the interaction least amenable to dose adjustment.
meaning.falsification_test: If induction effects are reported only as model predictions rather than administered studies the determination basis is predicted and must be recorded as such; the claims flag one such projection explicitly.
meaning.rationale: The cited quotes give measured losses of 50, 72, 77, 80, 85 and 87 percent for agents of this class, and a roughly ten-fold loss for one agent, which is why the definition states the fold-to-percentage conversion rather than letting a fold and a percentage share one axis. They also state that the ability to compensate by dose escalation is agent-dependent and not always supported, so avoidance is generally recommended, and that strong inducers of this enzyme should be avoided with some agents of the class while another tolerates them, which shows the quantity is agent-specific rather than generic. The axis carries induction losses only: a quote about dietary or herbal inhibition of the same enzyme describes the opposite perturbation, supports no value here, and is no longer cited. Loss of exposure is the failure mode that silently removes the target coverage this screen selects for, and no cited quote states an acceptable loss, so the rule is an ordering with no cutoff.

meaning.definition: The ratio of the compound's systemic exposure (AUC) with a strong CYP3A inhibitor to its exposure without one, always expressed as a value of at least 1, taken from an administered clinical interaction study and recorded with the index inhibitor, its dose and duration, the victim dosing design, the population studied and the endpoint reported. Percentage increases are converted before entry: a 51 percent increase enters as 1.51 and a 141.79 percent increase enters as 2.42, and no value may be entered as a bare percentage. Where a source reports both a model-based prediction and an administered study, only the measured ratio is entered and the prediction is recorded as a prediction; a source offering a prediction alone yields unknown. A peak-concentration ratio is a different endpoint and is recorded rather than entered. Because the cited evidence states that interaction studies differ in index perpetrator, dose and duration, in whether the victim drug was given as a single dose or at steady state, in the population studied and in the endpoint reported, so that a larger reported fold change does not by itself establish that one agent is more interaction-prone than another and the values are best used as an indication of the order of magnitude, the comparison this attribute supports is coarse by construction: candidates whose ratios fall within the same order of magnitude are not separated by this attribute, and a ranking that would turn on a within-order difference is routed to a human rather than scored. A ratio near 1 is best. Where no administered study exists the attribute returns unknown, which carries no penalty and leaves the candidate unranked here rather than scored as insensitive; that a compound is a known substrate of the enzyme is recorded as an annotation, because no cited quote supports a number for the untested case.
meaning.expected_change: Candidates whose exposure barely moves with a strong inhibitor rank above candidates whose exposure multiplies by an order of magnitude, the ranking no longer depends on whether a source wrote a fold or a percentage, candidates separated only within an order of magnitude are not ordered by this attribute, and candidates with no administered study are unranked here with their substrate status recorded.
meaning.falsification_test: Re-derive every value from the source's own numbers and confirm the conversion. If the index inhibitors, doses and designs differ too widely the ratios are comparable only as orders of magnitude; and if the top-ranked candidates prove to be those with no dedicated study, the untested flag is not working and the attribute must be restricted to studied candidates.
meaning.rationale: The cited quotes supply a graded series of measured results for this exact experiment, which after conversion to one scale runs from no clinically meaningful change through roughly 1.5-, 1.7-, 1.8-, 2.4- and 3.4-fold to 5.2- and 24-fold, together with the clinical consequence at the top of that range: co-administration of a strong inhibitor of this enzyme with one multi-kinase agent led to hepatic failure and death in a reported patient, and labels mandate defined dose reductions where co-administration is unavoidable. One cited quote states a model-based prediction of up to 16-fold alongside an administered study measuring 24-fold on exposure, which is why only the administered value is entered and the prediction is recorded as such. A further cited quote is the counter-evidence that sets the resolution of this attribute: interaction studies differ in index perpetrator, dose, duration, victim dosing design, population and endpoint, a larger reported fold change does not by itself establish that one agent is more interaction-prone than another, and such values are best used as an indication of the order of magnitude. That is why every value carries those design qualifiers, why the quantity is not treated as finely comparable between candidates, and why a ranking turning on a within-order difference goes to a human. Because the sources express the same measurement sometimes as a fold and sometimes as a percentage the conversion is specified, and because no quote states an acceptable ratio the rule is an ordering with no cutoff.

matching_facets.statement: the four facets of the recovery rubric (handoff §12.2), read from executing fields; `gaps` lists what the records do not say

meaning.definition: The median expert-curated affinity of the compound at fibroblast growth factor receptor 1, on the pChEMBL scale, that is the negative base-ten logarithm of the molar half-maximal inhibitory concentration, inhibition constant or dissociation constant as the curation reports it. Higher is better. The source bound here is an expert curation independent of the activity table that the registry's potency criterion for this receptor reads, and it can cover compound-target pairs that table lacks, which is the gap this attribute is for: a candidate whose engagement of this receptor is absent from one curation may be quantified in the other. It is therefore not a restatement of the registry criterion and does not replace it. The two read different sources, the median is taken over the records this source returns rather than a maximum, because a maximum rises with the number of records, and the action type and any selectivity comment travel with each record for a narrative to cite. Where the two curations disagree materially about the same compound the conflict is routed to a human rather than averaged. Absence of a record gives unknown and never a failure, because this curation is sparse outside developed and late-stage drugs.
meaning.expected_change: Candidates whose affinity at this receptor is quantified by a curation independent of the activity table are ranked on that measurement, which recovers coverage evidence for candidates the activity table does not cover, while candidates with no record in either curation are not penalised.
meaning.falsification_test: Compare this curation's values with the registry potency criterion for the same receptor across the pool. If the two agree everywhere and cover the same candidates, this attribute adds nothing and should be merged into that criterion; if they disagree materially for a candidate, the conflict is routed to a human rather than averaged. If the curation returns no record for any candidate the attribute yields only unknowns.
meaning.rationale: This is a required receptor, and the cited quotes show that nominal and real coverage of it differ: an approved oral inhibitor of the family exists, overexpression of this receptor is tied to disease biology, adding coverage of it to a vascular-receptor backbone is described as supplying an additional antiangiogenic mechanism, one agent potent at the vascular receptors is stated to inhibit it only weakly, and another is reported to inhibit it with low nanomolar potency. A quantified affinity separates documented engagement from an unquantified family-level mention, which is exactly the distinction the weak-inhibition quote shows matters. The mechanism-of-action record source this attribute previously read stamps every claim it returns with determination basis curated, a basis excluded by the bases an attribute here accepts, so every record it returned would be set aside at assessment time and the attribute would carry no evidence at all; that is the finding this revision answers. The attribute is therefore bound instead to the independent expert curation of affinity at this receptor, which returns measured values on the pChEMBL scale and, being independent of the activity table, reaches compound-target pairs that table lacks, the same gap the record-based form was meant to close, while stating how strongly rather than only that engagement is documented. No cited quote states a required affinity at this receptor, so the rule is an ordering with no cutoff, and an absent record is unknown rather than a failure.

The blocking finding is accepted and fixed at the scale. Pooling a doubling recorded as the number 2 with a 20 percent increase recorded as the number 20 made the smaller effect score ten times worse, inverting the ranking mechanically. The attribute now defines a single quantity, the fed-to-fasted exposure ratio expressed so that it is always at least 1, with percentage changes converted explicitly before entry: a 20 percent increase enters as 1.20 and a doubling as 2.0. The second material finding is fixed by the same construction, since taking the larger of the two ratios means a food-driven reduction in exposure is scored as a deviation of the same size as an equivalent increase, so under-exposure is no longer rewarded by a signed lower_better scale. The third finding is accepted and resolved by deleting the appeal to a non-cited warning from the falsification test rather than by adding a claim the item never cited; the test now states the comparability problem in its own terms.

operational_quantity.quantity_name: Food effect on systemic exposure as a fold deviation

matching_facets.statement: the four facets of the recovery rubric (handoff §12.2), read from executing fields; `gaps` lists what the records do not say

meaning.definition: The fold change in systemic exposure (AUC) between the fed and fasted states, expressed as a ratio of at least 1 in whichever direction the effect runs: the fed-to-fasted ratio where food increases exposure and the fasted-to-fed ratio where food decreases it, so the quantity measures the size of the prandial effect and not its sign. Percentage changes in exposure are converted before entry, a 20 percent increase entering as 1.20 and a doubling as 2.00, and no value may be entered as a bare percentage. A ratio of fed to fasted absolute bioavailability is a different quantity on a different endpoint and is not admitted here, and no conversion between the two is attempted; such a figure is recorded with the oral bioavailability attribute instead. Each value is recorded with the study population, the dose and whether dosing was single or at steady state, the caloric and fat content of the test meal, the analyte measured and the exposure endpoint reported, because the cited evidence states that values drawn from studies differing in those respects are not the output of a common experiment and should not be read as strictly comparable measurements. Values from studies differing in those respects are therefore not pooled: a label-derived value measured against a standard meal is preferred where one exists, and an unresolved disagreement between designs is routed to a human rather than averaged. A value of 1.00 means exposure is unaffected by food and is the best score; larger values are worse whether the effect is an increase or a decrease.
meaning.expected_change: Candidates whose exposure is insensitive to the prandial state score near 1.00 and rank above candidates requiring strict fasting or a specified meal composition; a candidate whose exposure falls with food is penalised as much as one whose exposure rises; and candidates whose only values come from incomparable study designs are routed to a human rather than ranked against each other.
meaning.falsification_test: Re-derive every value from the source's own numbers and check the conversion. If food-effect studies for the candidates used different meal compositions, analytes or dosing designs, the ratios are not strictly comparable between candidates and the attribute must be restricted to label-derived values measured against a standard high-fat meal.
meaning.rationale: The cited quotes span the whole range of this property and show it dictates the dosing instruction in both directions. A meal approximately doubles exposure for one multi-kinase agent, which must be dosed fasting; another must be taken with a specifically low-fat meal because both high-fat meals and fasting lower active-metabolite exposure; food increases exposure by roughly 20 percent for another with delayed absorption; one agent has 98 percent bioavailability regardless of food; and several show no effect and may be taken either way. Because effects run in both directions the quantity is unsigned, and because the same quotes report some effects as folds and others as percentages the conversion is specified rather than left to the reader. A further cited quote states that the food-effect studies these values come from differ in population, dose, single-dose versus steady-state design, meal composition, analyte and endpoint, and that descriptions of relative size should not be read as strictly comparable measurements; that quote is what the recorded qualifiers and the refusal to pool across designs implement. The axis carries exposure ratios only. A fed-versus-fasted change in absolute bioavailability is a different endpoint, no quote reporting one is cited here, and any such figure belongs to the oral bioavailability attribute, which records the prandial state with each value.

'count of kinases' aggregated by median across panels whose size the definition itself requires recording: a count from the 371-kinase screen in claim_01M4TXQQ0TQNSH090AG6QEDW7Z is not commensurable with one from a small panel.

The material finding is accepted: a bare count of inhibited kinases cannot be pooled by median across panels of different size, since three hits in a 371-kinase screen and three in a small panel are not the same observation. The measured quantity is therefore changed from a count to the fraction of the screened panel that is inhibited at or above the panel's own stated threshold, expressed as a percentage, which is commensurable across panels and keeps the attribute's meaning exactly. The definition now requires the panel size and the inhibition threshold to be recorded with each value and admits only panels that report both, and the rationale states that values from panels using different inhibition thresholds remain only loosely comparable. Citations are unchanged, and the 371-kinase quote now serves as the worked example of a value this attribute can actually compute.

The quote gives per-kinase percentages ('CLK1 (61.85%), LCK (44.62%), MAP3K19 (43.35%), and Aurora B (42.71%)') but states neither the panel size nor the screening threshold, both of which the definition requires before a value is admitted; it therefore yields no admissible value.; Of the six cited claims only claim_01M4TXQQ0TQNSH090AG6QEDW7Z can produce a value. claim_01M4TY6CMDHEX119N8WY36JMGF ('only a limited number of undesired targets'), claim_01M4TY6CPYRG6P7ZZ33EWG5CK6 ('a limited number o

Citation narrowed to the one quote that can yield a value, a 371-kinase screen with three kinases at or above 50 percent inhibition; the qualitative target lists, including the per-kinase percentages with no panel denominator or threshold, are removed. The definition now requires the panel's composition to be stated and recorded alongside size, screening concentration and threshold, and forbids pooling fractions from panels of different composition, routing such a disagreement to a human instead.

The admission rule now requires four qualifiers, but the single supporting quote supplies only two: 'only FGFR2, FGFR3 and ROS showing >=50% inhibition in a 371-kinase screen' states the panel size and the threshold and states neither the screening concentration nor the panel composition. On the tightened rule the attribute's own and only cited value is inadmissible.

The admission rule is brought back to what the evidence can state: a value needs the panel size and the inhibition threshold, which the cited 371-kinase screen gives, while the screening concentration and panel composition are recorded when stated and recorded as a gap when not, instead of being conditions that made the attribute's only cited value inadmissible. Non-comparability is handled where it belongs: fractions from panels differing in composition or concentration, or with those unstated, are not pooled and a comparison that would decide the ranking is routed to a human.

operational_quantity.quantity_name: Fraction of a profiling panel inhibited outside the required target set

matching_facets.statement: the four facets of the recovery rubric (handoff §12.2), read from executing fields; `gaps` lists what the records do not say

meaning.definition: Of the kinases screened in a profiling panel, excluding the five required receptors, the percentage inhibited at or above the panel's own stated threshold (for example 50 percent inhibition at the screening concentration). A value is admitted where the source states the panel size and the inhibition threshold, both of which are recorded with it, since without a denominator and a threshold no percentage exists. The screening concentration and the composition of the panel are recorded whenever the source states them and their absence is recorded as a gap, because a fraction is weaker evidence without them. Expressing the result as a fraction of the panel rather than as a raw count makes panels of different size commensurable; it does not make panels of different composition or screening concentration commensurable, because a panel enriched for the compound's own kinase family inflates the fraction for that compound. Fractions from panels that differ in composition or concentration, or whose composition or concentration is unstated, are therefore not pooled, and a comparison between them that would decide the ranking is routed to a human rather than averaged. Lower is better.
meaning.expected_change: Candidates that leave most of a large screened panel untouched rank above candidates with broad residual activity, and the ranking no longer depends on how many kinases each source happened to screen.
meaning.falsification_test: If the admitted panels differ in inhibition threshold, screening concentration or composition, the fractions are not comparable and the attribute must be restricted to a single panel convention or withdrawn. If only one candidate in the pool has a panel reported with all four qualifiers, the attribute ranks nothing and should be withdrawn at the merge stage.
meaning.rationale: One cited quote both demonstrates the quantity and fixes its convention: an agent is reported as sparing most of the kinome, with only three kinases showing at least 50 percent inhibition in a 371-kinase screen. That example is why the quantity must be a fraction rather than a count: three hits in a 371-kinase screen would otherwise be indistinguishable from three hits in a twenty-kinase panel. It states a panel size and an inhibition threshold, which is what a percentage needs and what the definition requires of every admitted value; it does not state the screening concentration or the panel's composition, which is why those are recorded when given and recorded as a gap when not, rather than being made conditions of admission that this evidence cannot meet. The qualitative off-target descriptions previously cited can yield no percentage, since a phrase such as a limited number of undesired targets, or a list of inhibited kinases with per-kinase percentages but no denominator and no threshold, has no denominator at all. Nothing in the cited evidence states a permissible fraction, so the rule is an ordering with no cutoff, and because composition and concentration are often unstated the attribute cannot settle a close comparison on its own.

meaning.definition: The number of hydrogen-bond donor groups in the molecule, taken as the computed descriptor for the neutral parent structure (the hydroxyl and amine hydrogens that the cited source names as the polar functional groups which increase solvation). Reported as an integer count. Fewer donors is scored as better, monotonically and with no threshold, because the cited claims support a direction of effect on membrane permeability but state no permissible number of donors. Two limits are part of the definition. The cited evidence describes a trade-off rather than a one-way preference: incorporating polar or ionisable groups improves aqueous solubility while raising polar surface area and reducing passive diffusion, so a monotone preference for fewer donors captures only one side of it, and this attribute is subordinate to the measured oral bioavailability attribute and must not outweigh it. And the value is a computed descriptor, a derived quantity rather than a measurement, so where a measured oral bioavailability exists for the same candidate the measurement governs and this attribute serves only to separate candidates that have none.
meaning.expected_change: Among candidates of comparable size and lipophilicity, those carrying fewer hydroxyl and amine donors rank higher on expected passive absorption, which separates scaffolds whose polarity sits in acceptors from those carrying many donors. Because the rule is an ordering with no cutoff, no candidate is excluded on this attribute and a candidate with a high donor count but a measured high oral bioavailability is not demoted below one with a favourable descriptor and no measurement.
meaning.falsification_test: Compute donor count and topological polar surface area for every candidate in the pool and correlate them. If the two rank the pool identically, they are one measurement and this attribute should be merged into the polar-surface-area attribute at the merge stage. Independently, if candidate ordering by donor count inverts the ordering by measured absolute oral bioavailability, the descriptor is not tracking absorption for these molecules and the attribute should be withdrawn in favour of the measured value.
meaning.rationale: The cited claims make donor count a determinant of absorption in its own right rather than a restatement of polar surface area: one states that lower polarity is associated with enhanced passive diffusion, evidenced by polar surface area below approximately 90 square angstroms together with a limited number of hydrogen-bonding interactions; a second states that an excess of polar functional groups, particularly hydroxyl and amine moieties, increases solvation and reduces membrane permeability; a third gives the design response, lowering polar surface area by bioisosteric capping; and a fourth lists hydrogen-bonding capacity alongside molecular weight and lipophilicity as the parameters whose modulation promotes oral bioavailability. Two limits follow from those same quotes and are recorded here rather than left implicit. The quoted threshold language is reported for central-nervous-system penetration, not for intestinal absorption, so it supports the direction of the effect but cannot license a numeric cutoff for this objective, which names no central-nervous-system compartment. And the value is a computed descriptor, a derived quantity rather than a measurement, so where a measured oral bioavailability exists for the same candidate the measurement governs and this attribute serves only to separate candidates that have none. A third consideration is now admitted here on the same terms as in the polar-surface-area attribute, since donor count and polar surface area express one polarity mechanism: the cited evidence states that incorporating polar or ionisable groups improves aqueous solubility while raising polar surface area and reducing passive diffusion, so fewer donors is not uniformly better, and the preference is weak and subordinate to measured absorption.

meaning.definition: The proportion of treated patients developing proteinuria of any grade, as a percentage, with the control-arm rate recorded where a randomised comparison reports one. The any-grade rate is the scored severity because it is the one the cited evidence resolves: the pooled any-grade difference is reported with a risk ratio and a confidence interval excluding unity, whereas the grade 3 or higher rate is reported as uncommon, not significantly different between groups, and with wide confidence intervals because of the low number of events. The grade 3 or higher rate is therefore recorded alongside every value, never entered, and never used to separate candidates. Reported renal pathology such as podocytopathy or thrombotic microangiopathy is a narrative finding rather than a percentage and is recorded rather than entered. Lower is better. Because the cited evidence associates renal dysfunction with inhibition of the required vascular receptor pathway, the rate counts against a candidate only where coverage of those receptors is comparable, and a low rate in a candidate whose coverage is weaker is routed to a human rather than credited.
meaning.expected_change: Candidates with lower any-grade proteinuria rates at comparable coverage of the required receptors rank above candidates in whom it is common, the severe-grade rate and the control-arm rate stay in the record, and no candidate is separated from another on severe-grade differences the cited evidence calls imprecise.
meaning.falsification_test: The claims record physiological proteinuria as a confounder of renal safety monitoring in some settings; if reported rates do not distinguish drug-induced from background proteinuria the attribute is biased and must be restricted to controlled comparisons.
meaning.rationale: The cited quotes quantify this across the class and against controls: any-grade proteinuria in 27.30 percent of treated patients compared with 16.19 percent of control patients, a pooled risk ratio of 1.89 with a confidence interval of 1.30 to 2.74, and 18.7 percent proteinuria with 2.4 percent high-grade across trials of this inhibitor class. The second cited quote is why the scored severity is the any-grade rate rather than the severe one: it states that grade 3 or higher proteinuria was uncommon, did not differ significantly between treatment groups, and carries wide confidence intervals because of the low number of events, so an ordering built on those severe-grade differences would rank candidates on an effect the evidence does not resolve. The severe rate is kept in the record because it is what prompts dose modification in practice. The substantial control-arm rate is why the control value is recorded with each measurement, and no cited quote states an acceptable rate, so the rule is an ordering with no cutoff.

meaning.definition: The proportion of treated patients developing central serous retinopathy, at any grade, as a percentage, reported for the compound itself. Two admission rules follow from the cited evidence. A rate is admitted only where the source reports it for a named molecule; a rate given for a drug class as a whole, such as a class table row of ocular event rates with no molecule named, is recorded as class context and is never entered as a candidate's value, which is why the two figures in the evidence, about 21 percent for a named agent in one indication and about 9 percent in a class table, are not two values for one axis. And every admitted value is recorded with the indication and the trial population it comes from; values from different indications are not pooled into one median, and where a candidate has values from more than one indication each is kept with its own label for a later stage to read. The grade 3 or higher rate is recorded alongside where a source reports one, and the severity entered is always the any-grade rate so that two severities never share the axis. The other ocular events in the evidence, retinal pigment epithelial detachment, retinal detachment, dry eye and cataract, are separate endpoints with their own rates and are recorded rather than entered. Whether baseline and periodic ophthalmological examination is mandated is a categorical requirement with no scale; it is recorded with the value as a monitoring burden for a human to weigh, and is not scored. Lower is better.
meaning.expected_change: Candidates with a lower central serous retinopathy incidence rank above candidates in whom it is common, with the other ocular event rates, the grade 3 figure and the ophthalmological monitoring mandate visible in the record rather than mixed into one percentage.
meaning.falsification_test: If ocular rates are drawn from a different indication or dose than the candidates would use they do not transfer; and because the claims describe this toxicity as reversible on discontinuation, severity should be weighted by reversibility rather than incidence alone.
meaning.rationale: The cited quotes identify this as a distinctive toxicity of the fibroblast growth factor receptor arm of the required coverage and quantify it in two different forms. One reports central serous retinopathy in 21 percent of patients, 3 percent at grade 3, for a named agent in trials of one indication; the other is a class table row giving about 9 percent for central serous retinopathy alongside about 20 percent dry eye, 4 percent retinal detachment and 6 percent cataract, with no molecule named. Those two figures differ more than twofold, and the definition now explains why that is not a conflict on one axis: the first is a candidate value from a stated indication, the second is class context, and only the first kind is entered. Recording the indication with every admitted value keeps the remaining population difference visible instead of averaging it away. The class table is retained in the support because it is the evidence that the other ocular endpoints exist and carry their own rates, and because it states the baseline eye examination and the interruption rule that the monitoring annotation records. No cited quote states an acceptable rate, so the rule is an ordering with no cutoff, and because the cited evidence describes this toxicity as reversible on discontinuation, the recorded reversibility must be read with the incidence.

matching_facets.statement: the four facets of the recovery rubric (handoff §12.2), read from executing fields; `gaps` lists what the records do not say

meaning.definition: The proportion of treated patients developing grade 3 or higher hypertension, as a percentage. Only the grade 3 or higher rate is entered; an any-grade rate is a different quantity, differing from it by around a factor of three in the same source, and is recorded alongside rather than entered, as is the control-arm rate where a randomised comparison reports one. This is the index on-target vascular toxicity of inhibiting the required vascular receptors, and the cited evidence states that their pharmacologic inhibition predictably produces a characteristic spectrum of toxicities. The measured rate is therefore recorded and weighed as a judgement against the candidate's coverage of those receptors rather than ordering the pool: a lower rate counts in a candidate's favour only where its coverage of the required vascular receptors is comparable, a low rate in a candidate whose coverage is weaker is routed to a human, and the attribute never ranks a candidate downward for an anticipated consequence of the coverage the objective requires. Because the judgement is on the rate together with the coverage, the rule carries no monotone ordering over the pool and no cutoff; the percentage, its severity grade, the control-arm rate and the candidate's coverage are what the human sees.
meaning.expected_change: The measured severe hypertension rate is surfaced for every candidate alongside its coverage of the required vascular receptors, so a human can see where a low rate reflects tolerability and where it reflects weaker engagement, and no candidate is ranked downward for an anticipated consequence of the coverage the objective requires.
meaning.falsification_test: Because hypertension is on-target, a candidate with no hypertension signal may simply not be engaging the vascular receptors; a zero rate must be cross-checked against the coverage criteria rather than rewarded on its own.
meaning.rationale: This is the most consistently quantified toxicity in the claim set and the one most tightly bound to the required targets. A meta-analysis of randomised trials of a selective inhibitor of the three required vascular receptors found any-grade hypertension in 34.92 percent versus 7.55 percent of controls and grade 3 or higher in 13.96 percent versus 1.21 percent, a risk ratio of 9.01, with zero between-study heterogeneity; in one disease subgroup the figures rose to 43.02 and 17.28 percent. Other agents of the class show 24.8 percent grade 3 to 4, 13.6 percent, 12 percent and 12.9 percent. The mechanism is stated too: the receptor pathway is required for adequate nitric oxide production, so its inhibition raises systemic vascular resistance, which makes this toxicity inseparable from the required coverage rather than an avoidable off-target effect. Because the cited evidence ties this toxicity mechanistically to inhibition of the required receptor pathway and calls the resulting toxicity spectrum predictable, a monotone preference on it would reward weaker engagement of a required target. The rule is therefore an exploratory consideration: the measured rate is surfaced for a human to weigh against the coverage criteria, and the definition states that it discriminates only between candidates of comparable coverage. Only the grade 3 or higher rate is entered, because the same source reports an any-grade rate three times larger and the median would otherwise be taken over two severities.

meaning.definition: The number of the three graded severities of hepatic impairment, mild, moderate and severe, at which the label or clinical pharmacology data for the compound state that a dose reduction is required or that use is not advised or contraindicated: an integer from 0 to 3. A grade counts as unrestricted only where the source reports pharmacokinetic or clinical data at that grade showing that no adjustment is needed. A label that simply contains no dosage adjustment for hepatic impairment is the absence of a labelled finding rather than a demonstrated absence of restriction, so every grade it does not address is recorded as untested and counted neither as restricted nor as unrestricted; a candidate whose only statement is of that kind therefore returns unknown rather than a count of zero. Where a source both restricts a grade and reports that grade as not well studied, the grade counts as restricted and is additionally flagged as restricted on untested grounds, because the restriction is the operative statement for dosing while the flag records that it rests on absent data rather than on measured exposure. The grade or grades restricted, the nature of each restriction, reduction or prohibition, and the number of grades actually covered are recorded with the count, so a partial count is never read as a complete one. Only data for an orally administered small molecule of the kind this objective concerns are used; a statement about a parenterally administered biological agent is outside the comparison and is not entered. Fewer restricted grades is better.
meaning.expected_change: Candidates with data at the graded severities showing no adjustment is needed rank above candidates restricted at several of them, a candidate whose label is merely silent returns unknown rather than a favourable count, and a grade restricted because it is unstudied is visible as such in the record.
meaning.falsification_test: If a candidate's hepatic-impairment data are absent, that is an untested restriction rather than an absent one, and the attribute must return unknown instead of a favourable score.

That pair of statements is why the definition now has a rule for a grade that is restricted precisely because it is unstudied: the grade counts as restricted, since that is what governs dosing, and carries a flag recording that the restriction rests on absent data. The quote whose only content is that a product label contains no dosage adjustment for hepatic impairment is no longer cited, on two grounds: the absence of a labelled finding is not a demonstrated absence of restriction, which is why such a grade is now recorded as untested rather than counted as unrestricted, and the agent it concerns is a parenterally administered biological rather than an orally administered small molecule, so it cannot calibrate the unrestricted end of this axis. meaning.definition: The number of the four renal function strata, mild, moderate and severe impairment and end-stage disease including dialysis, at which the source states for this compound that a dose reduction is required or that use is contraindicated or not recommended: an integer from 0 to 4. A stratum counts only where the source itself names it. A restriction stated purely as a measured cut, such as a creatinine clearance or filtration-rate figure with no stratum named, is recorded with its threshold and is not assigned to a stratum, because no cited quote supplies the correspondence between a numeric cut and the named strata; the strata such a restriction might cover are left untested in the count and the threshold travels with the value for a later stage to read. Where the source names a stratum and also gives its cut, for example end-stage disease with a stated filtration-rate figure, the restriction counts for that named stratum and the figure is recorded. A stratum for which the source reports no data is recorded as untested and counted neither as restricted nor as unrestricted, and a stratum counts as unrestricted only where the source states that no adjustment is needed for it. The count is reported with the number of strata actually covered, so a partial count is never read as a complete one. Only data for an orally administered small molecule of the kind this objective concerns are used, and an adherence or persistence measure is not a dosing restriction and is never counted. Fewer restricted strata is better.
meaning.expected_change: Candidates usable across the renal function strata rank above candidates restricted at several of them, with each stated threshold visible in the record, which matters because the cited evidence describes renal effects as an on-target consequence of inhibiting the required vascular receptors, so renal function may deteriorate on treatment.
meaning.falsification_test: Check that every counted restriction is stated for a named stratum and that strata with no data are recorded as untested. If most candidates have data for only one or two strata the counts are not comparable and must be reported with their coverage rather than ranked; if a candidate scores 0 only because no stratum has been studied, the attribute must return unknown instead of a favourable count.
meaning.rationale: The cited quotes give restrictions in the two forms this definition distinguishes. One names the strata directly: adjustment is not needed for mild to moderate impairment, while no data are available for severe impairment, stated with a creatinine clearance of 30 mL/min, or for end-stage renal disease, so two strata are unrestricted on reported data and two are untested. Another names a stratum and a cut together, use not recommended in end-stage renal disease at a stated filtration rate, alongside a contraindication stated only as a filtration-rate cut; the first counts for the named stratum and the second is recorded with its threshold rather than assigned to mild, moderate or severe, because nothing cited maps a numeric cut onto those names. The quotes also state that renal elimination of unchanged drug is comparatively minor for many agents of this class while the renal contribution is agent-specific, which is why this must be looked up for each candidate rather than assumed. A quote reporting consistent persistence rates across filtration-rate groups for a parenterally administered antibody has been removed from the support: persistence is an adherence measure rather than a dosing restriction, and the agent is outside the oral small-molecule comparison this objective concerns. meaning.definition: The number of the five required receptors for which a retrieved peer-reviewed or reference source states that this single molecule inhibits or binds the receptor. A receptor counts when the source names it either by its protein name or by an unambiguous gene symbol or long-standing synonym, namely CSF1R, c-FMS or FMS for the colony-stimulating-factor-1 receptor; VEGFR1 or FLT1; VEGFR2 or KDR; VEGFR3 or FLT4; and FGFR1. A statement that an agent covers a receptor family without naming the isoform counts for no isoform of that family, and a statement that qualifies the engagement at a receptor as weak, minimal, negligible or absent does not count that receptor as covered. Silence is not denial and not agreement: a retrieved source that does not mention a receptor neither adds it nor removes it, so a receptor counts where at least one retrieved source names it as engaged without qualification and no retrieved source denies or qualifies engagement at that receptor. A target list that omits a receptor therefore leaves a receptor counted from another source standing, while an explicit statement of weak, minimal or absent engagement removes it. Determination basis decides a conflict: where one source names a receptor and another reports engagement at it as weak or absent, a statement whose basis is measured governs over an asserted review target list. A receptor counted only from asserted target lists, with no measured statement either way, still counts, and the number of counted receptors resting on asserted lists alone is recorded with the value so that a count assembled from review strings is visible as such. An unresolved disagreement between sources of the same basis is routed to a human. The quantity is therefore an integer from 0 to 5 measuring how completely the retrieved sources name this molecule's coverage of the required set, not how potently it engages them.
meaning.expected_change: Candidates whose published target list names more of the five required receptors rank higher, and no candidate is excluded, so an agent described only at family level can still be recommended on the strength of the registry's measured potency criteria.
meaning.falsification_test: Score the pool and compare the ranking with the per-receptor potency criteria in the registry. If the two disagree systematically, this attribute is measuring publication practice rather than coverage and should be withdrawn. If every candidate scores the same, it discriminates nothing.
meaning.rationale: The objective is a single molecule engaging five named receptors at once, and the cited quotes show that agents in this class routinely cover only part of that set: some cover the three vascular receptors without the fibroblast growth factor receptor, one covers that receptor family alone without the vascular or macrophage receptors, one is potent at the vascular receptors but inhibits the required fibroblast growth factor receptor only weakly, and one is selective for that family with minimal activity at one of the vascular receptors. Counting the receptors a source actually names, and refusing to count the ones it names only to call the engagement weak or minimal, turns that partial-coverage pattern into a quantity without equating a weak mention with potent engagement. The two quotes that reach five receptors are asserted review target strings while the restrictive quotes are measured, which is why the definition now makes determination basis decide a conflict and records how much of a count rests on asserted lists alone: an asserted list can supply a receptor, but a measured statement of weak or absent engagement at that receptor overrides it. The same asymmetry is why silence is treated as neither agreement nor denial: a target list that happens not to mention a receptor is not evidence against it, and a count must not swing on which receptors a review chose to enumerate. It measures the completeness of reporting, so a source asserting family-level coverage without isoforms scores low and that low score is a statement about the source, not about the molecule; such a candidate is not excluded and its pharmacology is carried by the five per-receptor potency criteria already in the registry, which this attribute complements and never replaces.

meaning.definition: The number of the five required receptors for which engagement by this compound is supported by a direct measured readout, namely a biochemical or biophysical binding or inhibition assay, or a cellular target-engagement readout such as inhibition of receptor phosphorylation, reported for that receptor by name. Molecular docking, model-based predictions and unquantified narrative assertions do not count, and a receptor whose engagement a source reports as weak, minimal or absent does not count as measured engagement even where the statement is itself a measurement, because the count is of receptors shown to be engaged. Values are taken by consensus across the retrieved sources rather than from the most generous one: a receptor counts where a retrieved source reports a measured readout at it and no retrieved source of the same basis contradicts that, so one source asserting measurement at all five cannot set the count where other sources report only docking or prediction for some of them, and an unresolved disagreement is routed to a human. An integer from 0 to 5; higher is better.
meaning.expected_change: Candidates whose coverage of the required receptors is backed by measurement at more of those receptors rank above candidates whose target list is asserted or modelled, which guards the coverage counts against inflation by narrative review statements.
meaning.falsification_test: If determination basis cannot be read reliably from the retrieved text the count is guesswork and the attribute must be withdrawn rather than estimated; if every candidate scores 5 it discriminates nothing.
meaning.rationale: Two cited quotes state the rule this attribute enforces: docking-guided target assignment generates testable hypotheses about pocket accommodation but should not be presented as proof of direct inhibition without biochemical, biophysical or cellular target-engagement evidence, and where direct biochemical inhibition was not reported a compound should be regarded as a pathway modulator rather than a confirmed kinase inhibitor. Two further cited quotes are worked instances of what does count, both at required receptors and both on a measured basis: one agent is reported to inhibit the required fibroblast growth factor receptor together with two others of its family at low nanomolar inhibitory concentrations, and another is reported as a potent and selective inhibitor of all three required vascular receptors while inhibiting the fibroblast growth factor receptor only weakly. That pair also shows why the count must be per receptor and why a weak statement cannot count: the same source credits three receptors with measured potent engagement and one with weak engagement. Aggregation is consensus rather than a maximum, because a maximum would let one source asserting measurement at all five set the count while other retrieved sources report only docking for some of them, which is the same gap the coverage count closes. No cited quote states a required number of measured receptors, so the rule is an ordering with no cutoff.

Values are taken by consensus across sources that define the modification identically; the cited evidence states that reporting of dose intensity, reductions and discontinuation is inconsistent across trials and precludes quantitative pooling, so incomparably defined values are not pooled into one number and an unresolved disagreement is routed to a human. meaning.expected_change: Candidates whose effective dose can be sustained rank above candidates that most patients must step down from, linking this dimension back to delivered target coverage, with interruption, discontinuation and achieved dose intensity visible in the record rather than mixed into the score.

meaning.definition: The proportion of treated patients experiencing at least one grade 3 or higher adverse event, as a percentage, from clinical trials graded by standard criteria. The attribution is recorded with every value and fixes which quantity it is: a treatment-related rate and an all-cause rate are the same kind of proportion but not the same quantity, so they are never pooled into one median; the median is taken within an attribution, and where both exist for a candidate the treatment-related rate governs because it is the one attributable to the agent. Only a rate for events of any kind is admitted: the incidence of one named event, such as a single organ toxicity, is a different quantity and belongs to the organ-specific attributes. The predicate is a plain ordering on the absolute rate as reported, and it is always defined. What travels with every value, rather than suspending the ordering, is the context needed to discount it: the line of therapy, the trial population, and, for a randomised trial, the control-arm rate, because the cited evidence shows control-arm rates differing by about thirty points between these trials. A ranking that turns on values from different lines of therapy is therefore ordered as reported and flagged in the record as resting on different populations, so the human decision at recommendation time can see it; conflicting values for the same candidate under the same attribution are routed to a human. Lower is better.
meaning.expected_change: Candidates with lower severe-toxicity rates rank above candidates where three quarters of patients experience a grade 3 or higher event, which is the broadest single comparator the claims make available.
meaning.falsification_test: Severe-event rates depend on the line of therapy and the frailty of the enrolled population, which the claims show differ markedly between these trials; if the retrieved rates come from non-comparable populations they must be read as orders of magnitude only.
meaning.rationale: The cited quotes give values across agents of this class and show they span a wide range: 75.9 percent of patients with treatment-related grade 3 or higher events, all-cause rates of 61.1 and 62.7 percent against control-arm rates of 19.7 and 50.4 percent in the same trials, and 13 to 21 percent for a more selective agent. Those control arms are why the line of therapy, the population and the control-arm rate travel with every value: the same drug toxicity would otherwise look different according to the population enrolled. They are recorded as qualifiers rather than as a bar on comparison, because an attribute that refused to order most candidate pairs would rank nothing at all, and the rate as reported is still the best available summary of severe toxicity. The two attributions present in the quotes, treatment-related and all-cause, are why the definition fixes which is entered and forbids pooling them. The quotes also establish why this single number matters operationally, since grade 2 or greater events generally lead to dose interruption or reduction, and the standard grading system exists precisely to let consistent thresholds for dose adjustment and discontinuation be applied across trials. No cited quote states an acceptable rate, so the rule is an ordering with no cutoff.

meaning.definition: The change in the compound's own systemic exposure (AUC) when a transporter inhibitor or inducer is co-administered, expressed as a ratio of at least 1 in whichever direction the change runs, so that the same factor of change scores alike whether exposure rises or falls: a doubling and a halving both enter as 2.00. The conversion is stated because the sources report percentages: a percentage increase of X enters as 1 plus X divided by 100, so a 160.5 percent increase enters as 2.61, and a percentage decrease of Y enters as 1 divided by (1 minus Y divided by 100), so a 50.1 percent decrease enters as 2.00. A percentage is never entered as a bare number, and the direction of the change and the perturbing agent are recorded with every value. A statement about blood or plasma concentrations rather than exposure, and a peak-concentration change without an exposure change, are recorded rather than entered, because they are different endpoints. Where a source reports both an inhibitor arm and an inducer arm, both are converted and retained in the record; the scored value is the larger ratio, the worst perturbation in either direction, so an exposure loss is never discarded for being a loss but only for being the smaller movement on a scale that treats the two symmetrically. A value of 1.00 means exposure is unaffected and is the best score; larger values are worse.
meaning.expected_change: Candidates insensitive to transporter modulation score near 1.00 and rank above candidates whose exposure moves substantially with a transporter inhibitor or inducer, a rise and a fall of the same factor score alike, and a low cytochrome dependence is no longer mistaken for a low overall interaction liability.
meaning.falsification_test: If a candidate has a low cytochrome fraction and no transporter interaction study, its interaction liability is untested rather than low, and the attribute must return unknown rather than a favourable score.
meaning.rationale: The cited quotes show that for agents whose clearance avoids the cytochromes the interaction liability moves to transporters rather than disappearing: one agent metabolised mainly by a conjugating enzyme is nonetheless a transporter substrate whose exposure rose by 160.5 percent with a strong transporter inhibitor and fell by about 50 percent with an inducer, and one agent must have its dose halved with a potent transporter inhibitor. That single study is also why the scale is a fold deviation from unity rather than a percentage magnitude: on a percentage axis a doubling would enter as 100 and a halving as 50, so the same factor of change would score twice as badly as a rise as it does as a fall, and the two arms of that study are closer in factor than their percentages suggest. Converting both arms to a ratio of at least 1 makes a rise and a fall of the same factor score alike, which is the convention the food-effect attribute already uses. The quotes also record the converse case, an agent not substantially susceptible to either transporter or cytochrome interactions and therefore of minimal interaction potential, and none states an acceptable magnitude, so the rule is an ordering with no cutoff.

operational_quantity.quantity_name: Treatment discontinuation rate due to adverse events

matching_facets.statement: the four facets of the recovery rubric (handoff §12.2), read from executing fields; `gaps` lists what the records do not say

meaning.definition: The proportion of patients who permanently stopped treatment because of adverse events, as a percentage. A cessation rate that the source does not attribute to adverse events is a different quantity and is not admitted, and neither is a rate reported for a drug class other than the one under consideration. This measures whether the toxicity can be lived with, as distinct from how severe it is on paper. Each value is recorded with the line of therapy, because the cited evidence shows these trials differ in line and in the alternatives available to patients. Lower is better.
meaning.expected_change: Candidates patients can stay on rank above candidates abandoned by a third of their recipients, which is the practical meaning of tolerability for an agent meant to be taken continuously.
meaning.falsification_test: Discontinuation rates confound toxicity with the availability of alternatives: in a last-line setting patients persist with worse toxicity. If the retrieved rates come from different lines of therapy the comparison is unsafe.
meaning.rationale: The cited quotes supply a graded series of adverse-event discontinuation rates for agents of this class: about 10 percent, 14, 15.2 and 18.8 percent, and they record that one agent required dose reduction in 37 percent and discontinuation in 6 percent while another required reductions in 64.3 percent, interruptions in 66.2 percent and discontinuations in 18.8 percent. Since the objective is chronic oral dosing, the rate at which patients stop is a more faithful summary of tolerability than the graded event count. One quote previously cited has been dropped: it reports treatment cessation in approximately 5 percent of patients with operable and 36 percent with advanced disease for an unrelated inhibitor class, attributes the cessation to no cause, and reading it as an adverse-event discontinuation rate would add an attribution the quote does not make. No cited quote states an acceptable rate, so the rule is an ordering with no cutoff.

operational_quantity.quantity_name: VEGFR1 affinity on the independent expert curation

matching_facets.statement: the four facets of the recovery rubric (handoff §12.2), read from executing fields; `gaps` lists what the records do not say

meaning.definition: The median expert-curated affinity of the compound at vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 1, on the pChEMBL scale, that is the negative base-ten logarithm of the molar half-maximal inhibitory concentration, inhibition constant or dissociation constant as the curation reports it. Higher is better. The source bound here is an expert curation independent of the activity table that the registry's potency criterion for this receptor reads, and it can cover compound-target pairs that table lacks, which is the gap this attribute is for: a candidate whose engagement of this receptor is absent from one curation may be quantified in the other. It is therefore not a restatement of the registry criterion and does not replace it. The two read different sources, the median is taken over the records this source returns rather than a maximum, because a maximum rises with the number of records, and the action type and any selectivity comment travel with each record for a narrative to cite. Where the two curations disagree materially about the same compound the conflict is routed to a human rather than averaged. Absence of a record gives unknown and never a failure, because this curation is sparse outside developed and late-stage drugs.
meaning.expected_change: Candidates whose affinity at this receptor is quantified by a curation independent of the activity table are ranked on that measurement, which recovers coverage evidence for candidates the activity table does not cover, while candidates with no record in either curation are not penalised.
meaning.falsification_test: Compare this curation's values with the registry potency criterion for the same receptor across the pool. If the two agree everywhere and cover the same candidates, this attribute adds nothing and should be merged into that criterion; if they disagree materially for a candidate, the conflict is routed to a human rather than averaged. If the curation returns no record for any candidate the attribute yields only unknowns.
meaning.rationale: This is one of the required receptors and the cited quotes show it is covered as part of a set rather than alone: one approved oral agent inhibits it together with the other two vascular receptors and further kinases, a phase I agent covers it alongside two further kinases as an ATP-competitive inhibitor, the anti-angiogenic effect of the class is attributed to it and the second vascular receptor for angiogenesis and to the third for lymphangiogenesis, dual blockade of the first two suppressed angiogenesis and tumour growth in vitro, and one multikinase agent is recorded as lacking coverage of it altogether, so coverage here cannot be inferred from activity at the principal angiogenic receptor. The mechanism-of-action record source this attribute previously read stamps every claim it returns with determination basis curated, a basis excluded by the bases an attribute here accepts, so every record it returned would be set aside at assessment time and the attribute would carry no evidence at all; that is the finding this revision answers. The attribute is therefore bound instead to the independent expert curation of affinity at this receptor, which returns measured values on the pChEMBL scale and, being independent of the activity table, reaches compound-target pairs that table lacks, the same gap the record-based form was meant to close, while stating how strongly rather than only that engagement is documented. No cited quote states a required affinity at this receptor, so the rule is an ordering with no cutoff, and an absent record is unknown rather than a failure.
